exitCriterion: BitHire and The Management server-first paint already matches the settled tenant render with no dark or neutral flash
verdict: CLOSED for both binding tenant paths
theDefectHadThreeLinks: the DS default on bare :root is DARK — --ds-color-bg-primary #0A0A0C / --ds-color-bg-secondary #0F0F12 in foundation/themes/default.css; light and tenant values only activate through html-anchored selectors
the showroom's globals.css paints html background from --ds-color-bg-secondary, so the first frame resolved to #0F0F12

the probe route was a client page calling useSearchParams with no dynamic server API, so Next statically prerendered it and the whole subtree bailed out — the SERVED BODY WAS EMPTY, and the root element carried no data-* attributes at all
whyTheOldEvidencePathWasMisleading: the lab ran the real validator and compiler but inside a client component, kept only the normalized appearance, and mounted the provider with no visualAuthority — so the artifact's css was never embedded and the production compiled-artifact SSR path was bypassed entirely

theSeam.constraint: a page cannot own <html> and a layout cannot read searchParams, so the tenant can never reach the root element through JSX
theSeam.chosen: a first-in-body inline script stamping the resolved root attributes, plus an SSR-embedded <style> carrying the compiled artifact. Head stylesheets are render-blocking, so no paint can precede the stamp.
theSeam.whyNoSecondAuthority: the client providers CLAIM data-theme / data-tenant / data-engine (replace, restore on cleanup) rather than owning them, and the compiled-DB path declares compiled-artifact authority so the provider silences the channels the embedded artifact covers
theSeam.rootCause: awaiting searchParams on the server also removes the static-prerender bailout that was serving an empty body — the conversion is the cure, not a workaround

before.artifact: prerendered .next/server/app/probe/whitelabel-torture.html — ONE static file for every fixture

afterBithire.firstBodyChild: <script data-testid="probe-first-paint-stamp"> stamping data-theme=light, data-tenant=bithire, data-engine=modern, data-vertical=bithire, lang=en, dir=ltr

afterTheManagement.ordering: style at byte 7030, probe-ground at byte 10939 — the ground arrives before the content it grounds

servedBytes.buildOutput: the dispatcher and all 8 scene routes flipped from ○ (Static) to ƒ (Dynamic)

assertion.unitLayer: pnpm --filter @rottay/showroom test:first-paint -- --unit → 10 of 10, no build required
assertion.layers: 8 resolver assertions, 2 authority assertions, 17 fetched-HTML assertions against a real production build (next build + next start)
assertion.noCapturesUsed: R0 permits no browser captures; this asserts over the raw HTML string, which is the correct instrument — the veto is about bytes arriving without the tenant's ground, and a settled screenshot cannot see that frame

harnessProvenFalsifiable.law: a green assertion that cannot fail is not evidence
harnessProvenFalsifiable.evidence: the lane's FIRST run failed 3 of 25 on a real bug of its own — the stamp was sliced starting after the JSON payload, so data-tenant was never inside the slice
harnessProvenFalsifiable.vacuityFound: during that failure the 'no dark stamp' negative passed VACUOUSLY
harnessProvenFalsifiable.fix: both negatives now assert the stamp exists and declares a theme BEFORE asserting it is not dark
drills: two compiles of the same specimen yield one digest
dropping the compiled-artifact declaration falls back to provider authority with zero suppression — so the positive authority assertion is not vacuous

sceneRoutesCovered: all 8 stamp and server-render; scenes/primitives under the canonical-db tenant is inside the assertion and scenes/all was verified by hand

deliberateNonCoverage.reason: their CSS is compiled inside the provider at render time, so there is no ground to activate early. Stamping a scope would match nothing (torture-*) or newly activate the bithire vertical baseline (legacy management) and move that fixture's live snapshot baselines.
deliberateNonCoverage.consequence: ?fixture=torture-light still shows the DS default ground pre-hydration — unchanged from before this round, outside R0's binding objective, and not a regression

settledStateDomDelta.analysis: every bundle rule keyed on them was checked. The tenant artifacts' :where([data-ds-root][data-vertical='x']) arm is the same rule the html[data-tenant='x'] arm already matched, so :is() still resolves at (0,1,1); and :where([data-ds-root]) sets color, font-family and text-rendering at (0,0,0) on <html>, which body.showroom-site-body already overrides with the same three values.
settledStateDomDelta.conclusion: visually inert. The only other new DOM is one script and one style tag.
settledStateDomDelta.rtl: ?rtl=1 stamps lang=ar and dir=rtl, matching what the i18n provider settles to

openItemsNotBlocking: the frame still recompiles the specimen client-side rather than receiving the server's artifact by prop, because torture-sections/ was owned by another lane during this round. Both sides run the same pure function over the same frozen JSON and the assertion pins digest equality, so they cannot disagree — but the compile happens twice per request. The artifact prop already exists; threading it is a small change.

packages/core/dist/commercial.css was MISSING, which failed EVERY showroom build at probe/kit-inventory. It was regenerated with the core package's own build script — no source touched. Worth flagging: whoever last built core skipped build:commercial-css.

negativeDrill.violation: a served document whose first frame carries no tenant authority, or carries the DS default dark ground
negativeDrill.proof: packages/showroom/scripts/assert-first-paint-authority.mjs — the stamp must appear before probe-ground, must declare a theme, and must not be dark; the authority drill inverts the declaration and requires the fallback
